officialSource.adjudicationBasis: Read directly from the preserved official bytes. 18 Pa.C.S. § 3019(d)-(g) is a motion-to-vacate mechanism for a CLOSED conviction set — §§ 3503 (criminal trespass), 5503 (disorderly conduct), 5506 (loitering and prowling), 5507 (obstructing highways), 5902 (prostitution-related), or simple possession of a controlled substance — committed as a direct result of being a victim of human trafficking. (d)(2) requires the motion to be in writing, consented to by the attorney for the Commonwealth, describing supporting evidence with particularity, with entitling documents attached. (e) makes official victim documentation a presumption of the direct-result nexus, not a prerequisite. (f) directs that the court SHALL grant on the two findings. (g) mandates vacatur, striking the adjudication of guilt, and expungement of all related records. The compiled path-k pathway represents this mechanism at guidance depth — it names vacatur-plus-expungement for trafficking-connected convictions, screens with a non-coercive trafficking question, and routes to attorney escalation under a Lawrence hold — and asserts nothing the statute refutes. It does not encode the closed (d)(1) enumeration, the written-motion/consent/evidence requirements, the (e) presumption, or the (f) grant standard; those deltas are carried as a counsel-review requirement on the E4 row, never as a mapping change.

officialSource.adjudicationBasis: Read directly from the preserved official bytes. S.C. Code § 16-3-2020(F), as rewritten by 2024 Act No. 213 § 2 (eff July 2, 2024), grants a motion-based EXPUNGEMENT remedy: a victim of trafficking in persons convicted or adjudicated delinquent of a trafficking-article violation, prostitution, or any other nonviolent misdemeanor or Class F felony (defined by reference to § 16-1-20(A)(6)-(9)) may motion the court to expunge; the court may grant on a preponderance finding that participation was a direct result of, or interrelated to, being a victim of trafficking; reasonable notice must go to the original prosecuting agency and to victims per the Victim's Bill of Rights; Act 213 § 6 makes the SECTION 2 rights retroactive. The compiled pathway represents the current post-2024 mechanism in near-statutory language — victim status incl. adjudicated delinquent, the exact offense-class formula, the direct-result-or-interrelated nexus, the preponderance standard, the expungement remedy, and the minor-victim protection — and asserts nothing the statute refutes. It omits the two notice requirements and the express retroactivity note; those deltas are carried as a counsel-review requirement on the E4 row, never as a mapping change. The subsection's separate affirmative-defense clause is a prosecution-stage effect, distinct from the expungement remedy adjudicated here.
